text: {"edits": [{"finding_ids": ["app/tickets.py:11:config-class"], "search": "    model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)", "replace": "    model_config = ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True, coerce_numbers_to_str=True)", "explanation": "The test fails because Pydantic v2 no longer coerces int inputs to str for str fields (v1 did). The database returns integer ids, so ticket_id and assignee_id reject them. Setting coerce_numbers_to_str=True in the existing model_config restores v1's int-to-str coercion. This edit stays inside the Ticket model_config, next to the flagged config-class finding, and does not touch from_db_rows at line 16, which the rejected edit did."}], "notes": "The failed edit targeted line 16 (from_db_rows), which is outside the scope of the findings and imports, so it was rejected. This proposal fixes the failure in the model config instead. ConfigDict is already imported, and coerce_numbers_to_str is a ConfigDict option in Pydantic 2.x (2.4+), so no import changes are needed. It makes str fields accept int/float inputs and coerce them to str, matching v1 lax-mode behavior. The previous migration edits (ConfigDict, str_strip_whitespace) are kept as they are. Caveat: from_db_rows will now return ticket_id and assignee_id as strings such as \"101\" and \"7\". If the test expects the original integer values, the test or the field types would need to change, and that would be a separate decision."}
